question: A team defines a performance-optimizer subagent with the description 'Performance optimization specialist for query tuning' but never mentions the subagent by name in prompts. A user then asks the main agent to 'speed up this slow database query.' What determines whether the main agent delegates to this subagent?
options: A) The subagent is chosen at random among all defined subagents whenever the main agent's context window approaches its token limit
B) The subagent is invoked automatically whenever the Bash tool is present in the parent's allowed tool list, regardless of the task's subject matter
C) The subagent is invoked only if the user's prompt contains the exact subagent name, so this request would be handled by the main agent directly
D) Claude compares the task to each defined subagent's description field and automatically delegates when the task matches, without the user naming the subagent
correct_answers: D) Claude compares the task to each defined subagent's description field and automatically delegates when the task matches, without the user naming the subagent
explanations: Wrong — subagent selection isn't randomized or triggered by context window pressure; it's driven by matching the task to a subagent's description.
Wrong — subagent invocation depends on task-to-description matching, not on which tools happen to be present in the parent's allowed tool list.
Wrong — explicit naming guarantees invocation, but automatic invocation based on a matching description doesn't require the user to name the subagent at all.
Correct — Claude decides whether to invoke a subagent based on how well the task matches that subagent's description field, enabling automatic delegation without naming it.
